source_text: Disciplina custos spei, retinaculum fidei, dux itineris salutaris, fomes ac nutrimentum bonae indolis, magistra virtutis, facit in Christo manere semper ac jugiter Deo vivere et ad promissa coelestia et ad divina praemia pervenire. Hanc et sectari salubre est, et aversari ac negligere lethale. In Psalmis loquitur Spiritus sanctus: Continete disciplinam, ne forte irascatur Dominus, et pereatis a via recta, cum exarserit cito ira ejus super vos. Et iterum: Peccatori autem dixit Deus. Ad quid exponis justificationes meas, et assumis testamentum meum per os tuum? Tu autem odisti disciplinam et abjecisti sermones meos retro. Et denuo legimus: Disciplinam qui abjicit, infelix est. Et de Salomone mandata Sapientiae monentis accepimus: Fili, ne neglexeris disciplinam Domini, nec defeceris ab eo correptus; quem enim diligit Deus corripit. Si autem Deus quem diligit corripit et ad hoc corripit ut emendet, fratres quoque, et maxime sacerdotes, non oderunt sed diligunt eos quos corripiunt ut emendent. quando et Deus per Hieremiam ante praedixerit et tempora nostra significaverit dicens: Et dabo vobis pastores secundum cor meum, et pascent vos pascentes cum disciplina. Quod si in Scripturis sanctis frequenter et ubique disciplina praecipitur, et fundamentum omne religionis ac fidei de observatione ac timore profiscitur, quid cupidius appetere, quid magis velle ac tenere nos convenit, quam ut, radicibus fortius fixis, et domiciliis nostris super petram robusta mole solidatis, inconcussi ad procellas et turbines saeculi stemus, ut ad Dei munera per divina praecepta veniamus, considerantes pariter ac scientes quod templa Dei sint membra nostra, ab omni faece contagionis antiquae lavacri vitalis sanctificatione purgata, nec violari ea aut pollui fas sit, quando qui violat et ipse violetur. Eorum nos templorum cultores et antistites sumus. Serviamus illi cujus esse jam coepimus. Paulus in Epistolis suis dicit quibus nos ad curricula vivendi per divina magisteria formavit: Non estis vestri. Empti enim estis pretio magno. Clarificate et portate Deum in corpore vestro Clarificemus et portemus Deum puro et mundo corpore et observatione meliore; et qui per sanguinem Christi redempti sumus, per omnia servitutis obsequia Redemptoris imperio pareamus, demusque operam ne quid immundum et profanum templo Dei inferatur, ne offensus sedem quam inhabitat derelinquat. Sospitantis Domini verba sunt et docentis, curantis pariter et monentis: Ecce, inquit, sanus factus es, jam noli peccare, ne quid tibi deterius fiat. Dat vivendi tenorem, dat innocentiae legem, postquam contulit sanitatem; nec habenis liberis et solutis vagari postmodum patitur, sed ipsis potius quibus sanatus fuerat mancipato gravius comminatur, quod sit scilicet minor culpa deliquisse ante cum necdum nosses disciplinam Dei, nulla sit venia ultra delinquere postquam Deum nosse coepisti. Et quidem hoc tam viri quam mulieres, tam pueri quam puellae, sexus omnis atque omnis aetas observet, et curet, pro religione et fide quam Deo debet, ne quod sanctum et purum de Domini dignatione percipitur, minus sollicito timore teneatur. Nunc nobis ad virgines sermo est; quarum quo sublimior gloria est, major et cura est. Flos est ille ecclesiastici germinis, decus atque ornamentum gratiae spiritalis, laeta indoles, laudis et honoris opus integrum atque incorruptum, Dei imago respondens ad sanctimoniam Domini, illustrior portio gregis Christi. Gaudet per illas atque in illis largiter floret Ecclesiae matris gloriosa foecunditas; quantoque plus copiosa virginitas numero suo addit, tanto plus gaudium matris augescit. Ad has loquimur, has adhortamur affectione potius quam potestate; non quod, extremi et minimi et humilitatis nostrae admodum conscii, aliquid ad censuram licentiae vindicemus, sed quod, ad sollicitudinem magis cauti, ptus de diaboli infestatione timeamus. Neque enim inanis haec cautio est et vana formido quae ad salutis viam consulit, quae Dominica et vitalia praecepta custodit, ut quae se Christo dicaverint, et a carnali concupiscentia recedentes tam carne quam mente se Deo voverint, consumment opus suum magno praemio destinatum, nec ornari jam aut placere cuiquam nisi domino suo studeant, a quo et mercedem virginitatis expectant, dicente ipso: Non omnes capiunt verbum, sed illi quibus datum est. Sunt enim spadones qui ex utero matris sic nati sunt, et sunt spadones qui coacti sunt ab hominibus, et sunt spadones qui se ipsos castraverunt propter regnum coelorum. Denuo quoque per hanc Angeli vocem continentiae munus ostenditur, virginitas praedicatur: Hi sunt qui cum mulieribus se non coinquinaverunt. Virgines enim permanserunt. Hi sunt qui sequuntur Agnum quocumque ierit. Neque enim tantum masculis continentiae gratiam Dominus repromittit et feminas praeterit, sed, quoniam femina viri portio est et ex eo sumpta atque formata est, in Scripturis fere omnibus ad protoplastum Deus loquitur, quia sunt duo in carne una et in masculo simul significatur et femina.
pass_a_gloss: Discipline is the guardian of hope, the restraint of faith, the leader of the path of salvation, the nourishment of good character, the teacher of virtue, causing us to always remain in Christ and to live for God, and to attain the heavenly promises and divine rewards. It is healthy to follow this discipline, and deadly to reject and neglect it. The Holy Spirit speaks in the Psalms: Hold on to discipline, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the right path, when His anger blazes quickly over you. And again: To the sinner, God said, Why do you explain my justifications and take my covenant upon your lips? You, however, have hated discipline and rejected my words behind your back. We also read: Whoever rejects discipline is unhappy. And from Solomon's Wisdom, we have received the command: My son, do not neglect the discipline of the Lord, nor faint when He corrects you; for the one whom God loves, He corrects. If God, who loves, corrects and does so in order to improve, then brothers, and especially priests, do not hate but love those they correct so that they may improve. When God, through Jeremiah, foretold and indicated our times, saying: I will give you shepherds according to my heart, and they will feed you with knowledge and discipline. Since discipline is frequently and everywhere commanded in the Holy Scriptures, and the foundation of all religion and faith proceeds from its observation and fear, what should we more eagerly desire, what should we more strongly wish and hold, than that, with our roots more firmly fixed and our dwellings built on a strong rock, we may stand unshaken against the storms and whirlwinds of the world, so that we may come to God's gifts through divine precepts, considering and knowing that our bodies are temples of God, purified from all the filth of ancient contamination by the sanctification of the living water, and that it is not right for these to be violated or polluted. We are the cultivators and priests of these temples. Let us serve the One whose we have begun to be. Paul says in his Epistles, by which he formed us for the courses of living through divine teachings: You are not your own, for you have been bought with a great price. Let us glorify and carry God in our body; let us glorify and carry God with a pure and clean body and better observance; and we, who have been redeemed through the blood of Christ, let us obey the command of the Redeemer through all the services of servitude, and let us take care that nothing unclean and profane be brought into the temple of God, lest the Lord, who is offended, abandon the dwelling place He inhabits. The words of the Lord, who saves and teaches, who cares and warns, are: Behold, you have been healed, do not sin anymore, lest something worse happen to you. He gives the tenor of living, the law of innocence, after He has granted health; and He does not permit us to wander thereafter with loose and free reins, but rather threatens us more severely with the same things by which we were healed, because it is a lesser fault to have sinned before when we did not yet know the discipline of God, and there is no forgiveness for sinning after we have begun to know God. And indeed, this should be observed and cared for by both men and women, by both boys and girls, of all sexes and ages, for the sake of the religion and faith they owe to God, lest what is holy and pure, received from the Lord's dignity, be held with less solicitous fear. Now our speech is to virgins; whose glory is more sublime, their care is also greater. They are the flower of the Church's germination, the ornament of spiritual grace, a joyful character, a work of praise and honor, whole and uncorrupted, the image of God responding to the Lord's sanctity, a more illustrious part of Christ's flock. The glorious fertility of the Church, our mother, rejoices and flourishes abundantly through them; and the more numerous the virgins are, the more the mother's joy increases. We speak to them, we exhort them with affection rather than power; not because, being extremely humble and conscious of our humility, we claim any right to censure, but because, being more cautious, we fear the devil's temptation. For this caution is not empty and this fear is not vain, which consults the path of salvation, which keeps the Lord's and vital precepts, so that those who have dedicated themselves to Christ and, receding from carnal desire, have vowed themselves to God in both flesh and mind, may consummate their work, destined for a great reward, and may not strive to be adorned or pleasing to anyone except their Lord, from whom they also expect the reward of virginity, He Himself saying: Not all receive this word, but those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made so by men, and there are eunuchs who have castrated themselves for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Again, through the voice of the Angels, the gift of continence is shown, virginity is preached: These are those who have not defiled themselves with women. For they have remained virgins. These are those who follow the Lamb wherever He goes. For the Lord does not promise the grace of continence only to men and pass over women, but, since woman is a part of man and was taken and formed from him, in almost all the Scriptures, God speaks to the first-formed man, because the two are one flesh and the woman is signified in the man.

pass_b_english: Discipline is the guardian of hope, the restraint of faith, the guide of the path of salvation, the spark and nourishment of good character, the teacher of virtue; it makes us abide in Christ always and continually live for God, and reach the heavenly promises and divine rewards. It is healthy to follow this discipline, and deadly to reject and neglect it. The Holy Spirit speaks in the Psalms: "Hold fast to discipline, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the right way, when His wrath blazes quickly against you" (Psalm 2:12). And again: "To the sinner God said: Why do you recite My statutes, and take My covenant on your lips? For you have hated discipline and cast My words behind you." We also read: "Whoever rejects discipline is unhappy." And from Solomon's Wisdom, the command of the One who warns: "My son, do not neglect the discipline of the Lord, nor faint when you are corrected by Him; for whom the Lord loves He corrects" (Proverbs 3:11-12). If God corrects the one He loves, and corrects for the purpose of amendment, then brothers, and especially priests, do not hate but love those they correct so that they may amend. When God foretold through Jeremiah and signified our times, saying: "I will give you shepherds according to My heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and discipline" (Jeremiah 3:15). Since discipline is frequently and everywhere commanded in the Holy Scriptures, and the whole foundation of religion and faith springs from its observance and fear, what should we more eagerly desire, what should we more strongly wish and hold, than that, with roots more firmly fixed and our dwellings established on a strong rock, we may stand unshaken against the storms and whirlwinds of the world, so that we may come to God's gifts through divine precepts, considering and knowing that our bodies are temples of God, purified from all the filth of ancient contagion by the sanctification of the living water, and that it is not permissible for these to be violated or polluted, since whoever violates them will himself be violated? We are the cultivators and ministers of these temples. Let us serve the One whose we have begun to be. Paul says in his Epistles, by which he formed us for the courses of living through divine teachings: "You are not your own, for you were bought with a great price. Glorify and carry God in your body" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). Let us glorify and carry God with a pure and clean body and better observance; and we who have been redeemed through the blood of Christ, let us obey the Redeemer's command through all the services of servitude, and take care that nothing unclean and profane be brought into the temple of God, lest the offended Lord abandon the dwelling place He inhabits. The words of the Lord who saves and teaches, who cares and warns, are: "Behold, you have been made well; sin no more, lest something worse happen to you" (John 5:14). He gives the tenor of living, the law of innocence, after He has granted health; and He does not permit us to wander thereafter with loose and free reins, but rather threatens us more severely with the very things by which we were healed, because it is a lesser fault to have sinned before when we did not yet know the discipline of God, and there is no pardon for sinning after we have begun to know God. And indeed this should be observed and cared for by both men and women, by both boys and girls, of every sex and every age, for the sake of the religion and faith they owe to God, lest what is holy and pure, received from the Lord's dignity, be held with less solicitous fear. Now our speech is to virgins; whose glory is more sublime, their care is also greater. They are the flower of the Church's germination, the glory and ornament of spiritual grace, a joyful character, a work of praise and honor whole and uncorrupted, the image of God answering to the Lord's sanctity, a more illustrious portion of Christ's flock. The glorious fruitfulness of the Church our mother rejoices and flourishes abundantly through them and in them; and the more copious virginity increases by its number, the more the mother's joy grows. We speak to them, we exhort them with affection rather than power; not because, being the least and lowliest and keenly conscious of our humility, we claim any right to censure, but because, being more cautious in our solicitude, we fear the devil's assault. For this caution is not empty and this fear is not vain, which consults the way of salvation, which keeps the Lord's and vital precepts, so that those who have dedicated themselves to Christ and, withdrawing from carnal desire, have vowed themselves to God in both flesh and mind, may complete their work destined for a great reward, and may not strive to be adorned or pleasing to anyone except their Lord, from whom they also expect the reward of virginity, He Himself saying: "Not all can accept this word, but only those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made so by men, and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 19:11-12). Again also through the voice of the Angel the gift of continence is shown, virginity is preached: "These are they who have not defiled themselves with women; for they are virgins. These are they who follow the Lamb wherever He goes" (Revelation 14:4). For the Lord does not promise the grace of continence only to men and pass over women, but, since woman is a part of man and was taken and formed from him, in almost all the Scriptures God speaks to the first-formed man, because the two are one flesh and the woman is signified together with the man (Genesis 2:21-24).
